1.sofaString: 109	Pt, ******, is a 3 month old female[FP1] who is diagnosed with pulmonary atresia with intact ventricular septum with right ventricular dependent coronary circulation who is being referred for heart transplant Psychosocial Assessment[FP2].     Information for this assessment was obtained through an interview with the pt's parents and review of the medical records.   SW spent 60 minutes of face to face time with patient and family.     Living situation:  **, ******, lives with her parents, older brother, grandparents, aunt, uncle[FP3], and ******* in *******, *******.  They reside in a * ******* ********* with city water and central heating and a/c.  The air filters are replaced monthly[FP4].   There is no smoking in the home, although both parents report that they smoke outside[FP5]. They reside with ********'s parents and siblings currently[FP14].  However, they are hoping to relocate to Gainesville to be closer to the hospital, and to get their own housing[FP15].  *********, ********'s mother is keeping her 8 yr old son while they are here in Gainesville with the baby.  ******* states his family also resides in *******.  However, he states he is not involved with his family.  He states they are not supportive of him[FP16].       Financially, the family has very little support[FP17].  ******* reports that he does a lot of odd jobs, including moving furniture, fencing, and doing ********[FP18].  He states he is always able to provide what they need if given enough advance notice.  He states he does not mind working hard and will do whatever it takes to provide for his family.  However, he is somewhat limited because he does not have a drivers license currently[FP19].  He states he has to finish paying off a seatbelt fine, as he was stopped for a traffic violation and did not have ******* in a car seat[FP20].  He states he **** about $100 and will have his license reinstated when he is able to pay that.  ******** also does not have a drivers license[FP21].  It will be more expensive to get hers reinstated as she has to pay court fees.  She was driving on a suspended license and was cited for a traffic violation.  Neither of them own a car[FP22].       They have applied ****** for SSI but this is still pending[FP23].  ******** was supposed to go to an appt at the social security office in regards to this.  *******, ****** was then admitted.  SW provided phone number for her to call and request a telephone interview since pt is admitted out of ****.       ****** is covered by Medicaid[FP24] ********/ ********.  This may assist with displacement housing post-transplant.  This will also cover Medicaid transportation to and from medical appointments[FP25].       Fundraising to assist with these displacement expenses was discussed[FP26]. The family was given information on **** (Childrens ***** Transplant Association).  They were also given an application for First Hand Foundation[FP27] *****.         Both parents are legally permitted to sign consents and make medical decisions.  SW discussed how they handle situations regarding ****** if they are in disagreement about the decision.  Both state that they are typically able to discuss this and come to a consensus[FP28].      Course of illness:     ****** was diagnosed with her heart condition prenatally.  She is diagnosed with pulmonary atresia with intact ventricular septum and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy ********* with a PDA stent.  She had a heart cath in which LVH and RV dependent coronary circulation were identified.  As a result, she was referred to ** ****** for transplant evaluation     Financial Situation:     ****** is covered by Medicaid[FP29] ********/ ********.  The family has begun the process of applying for SSI for her[FP30].  The family receives WIC[FP31] and **********.  ******** is ordered to receive child support for her son, *******, but states she does not receive this[FP32].  Primarily, the family is supported by whatever work ******* is able to find.         Family History:     There is no reported medical history in the family other than a grandfather passing away in his 60s from a heart attack.    In addition, the family reports that they were expecting a child about 2 years ago and ******** had a miscarriage.     There is no reported mental health history other than ******** having postpartum depression with her first child[FP33].  She disclosed that this was partially related to DV issues with his father[FP34].  Psychotropic medication management of this was recommended, but she states she never took anything.  She denies any postpartum depression with ******.       The family denies any substance abuse history currently[FP35].  ******* disclosed that he did smoke ********* a few times when he was 18[FP36], and received a misdemeanor charge for this[FP37].  He denies any current usage.   ******** does report history of DV with father[FP38] of *******.  She reports continued problems with him.  ******* is still ordered to have visitation with him, although this is arranged through the grandmother.  ******** states she does not deal directly with him.  *******, ******* disclosed that they do receive threatening phone calls[FP39] from *******'s father at times, as well as ******* against ******.  ******** disclosed that DCF was involved when ******* was little due to these DV issues[FP40].  They deny any other history of involvement with DCF, law enforcement, arrests, or criminal history[FP41].       Adherence:  There are no concerns for adherence that have been documented at this time[FP42].  The family reports that they have been able to give ****** her meds and provide her care needs without difficulty during the brief times she has been at home in between her admissions.  They both state they are comfortable giving meds, checking weight and checking pulse ox.  They disclosed they were trained in how to check BP as well but were not provided a blood pressure cuff to do so[FP43][FP44].  ****** was feeding by mouth prior to admission, so they have not had to learn g-tube care. They verbalize belief that they will be able to do so if needed[FP45].  They report that they will be able to keep follow up appointments, even if they have to use Medicaid transportation.  Both appear bonded with ******.         Assessment and recommendations:     The family has very limited financial resources and tangible supports[FP46][FP47].  They do report adequate emotional support and support with care for the older child.  They verbalize a desire to move forward with transplant[FP48]. They report that it is 'scary' but they want the best opportunity[FP49] for ******.  *******, ******* also disclosed that he would like to be given information if ****** is ever at a point where it is not likely that she would be able to have a good life.  He states that he does not want her 'hooked up to machines forever' with no real hope of being able to come off of them.  He states that he does not feel that is really living, and would rather let her go if it gets to that point. He states he believes she is strong and will fight through, but wanted to express his thoughts on this should it come to it[FP50].  ******** expressed hope and belief that ****** will be ok, and states she would never want to have to make a decision about end of life care.          IMPRESSION:     (Low Risk - 1; Moderate Risk - 2; High Risk - 3; Severe Risk - 4)     Home Environment/Transportation -  3     Family Background & Social Support -  2     Financial/Insurance  - 2     Mental Health/Substance Abuse - 1     Involvement with *** Enforcement/Child Protection -  1     Adherence - 1     Understanding of medical situation & transplant process -  1     Health Literacy -  1     Coping Skills - 2     Total:  14  Moderate     The family scores as moderate risk in regards to psychosocial contra-indicators to transplant.       The biggest concern is the lack of financial support.  Recommendations are listed below:     Recommendations:  *Provide ongoing education about heart transplant and post-transplant care. Use teach-back method to ensure that the parents understand what is being explained.  *Provide fundraising and financial resources to assist the family with expenses that arise secondary to child's extended admission   *Assist with resources for local housing should the family continue to make plans to relocate to Gainesville permanently [FP51]       ****** ******** LCSW  Pediatric Heart/ Lung Transplant Team[FP1]gender[FP2]ACC_Health_Care[FP3]Living_Condition[FP4]Living_Supply[FP5]Smoking[FP6]Living_Condition[FP7]Education_General[FP8]IPV Historical[FP9]Employment_Status[FP10]Education_General[FP11]Occupation[FP12]Employment_Status[FP13]Social_Cohesion[FP14]Living Condition[FP15]Financial_Constraint[FP16]Social_Support[FP17]Poverty[FP18]Occupation[FP19]Financial_Constraint[FP20]Personal_Safety[FP21]Fianncial_Constraint[FP22]Financial_Constraint[FP23]Insurance[FP24]Insurance[FP25]Financial_Constraint[FP26]Financial_Constraint[FP27]Financial_Constraint[FP28]Social_Cohesion[FP29]Insurance[FP30]Insurance[FP31]Poverty[FP32]Poverty[FP33]Mental Health[FP34]IPV (Historical)[FP35]Drug_Abuse[FP36]Drug Abuse (Historical)[FP37]Legal Involvement[FP38]IPV[FP39]Personal_Safety[FP40]Abuse (Historical)[FP41]Abuse[FP42]Adherence[FP43]Adherence[FP44]Literacy[FP45]Literacy[FP46]Poverty[FP47]Social_Support[FP48]Literacy[FP49]Literacy[FP50]Literacy[FP51]Recommendations
